content.comment_body: Hello, I've searched through the forum but couldn't find a solution. I'm interested in knowing if the communication speed between [product_name] and a web page allows for high-resolution counter values (such as 0.01 seconds) to be displayed in real time on my PC via the internal web server of the device. Thanks!

I ran a test using a pulse generator from [product_name]. In this setup, a pulse is counted every 0.02 seconds and it's not possible to set a shorter period. You can refer to the attached video for details.

Thank you for your testing and feedback. I'm working on a project but don't currently have access to a [product_name]-module, so I couldn't check this myself. Based on your results, it appears that the web server displays resolution at 0.02 seconds instead of 0.01 seconds when using the stopwatch function.
You can attempt to use a 0.01-second interval. However, in my pulse generator example, the minimum achievable period was 0.02 seconds (composed of a 0.01 second pulse and 0.01 second pause).

analysis.insight_summary: Users are investigating if the web server on [product_name] is capable of transmitting high-frequency counter data (at 0.01-second intervals) to a PC in real time. Test results suggest the web server reliably shows updates at no faster than 0.02-second intervals, indicating restrictions in either the hardware, the web server implementation, or both, that limit real-time display of finer counter resolutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that the web server for [product_name] will support real-time display of high-resolution counter values (0.01s) on a connected PC, accurately reflecting the device's measurement capabilities.
